vision: First Elixir implementation of the Machine Payments Protocol — HTTP 402 payment middleware that turns any Phoenix API into an agent-billable service. No accounts, no API keys. Payment is authentication.

task.title: Challenge module
task.body: Challenge struct with HMAC-SHA256 binding. Challenge ID = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(secret, realm|method|intent|request|expires|digest|opaque)). Stateless — no challenge store needed; server recomputes and constant-time-compares on verification.
task.implemented: Shipped the Challenge struct with stateless HMAC-SHA256 binding — the challenge ID is base64url(HMAC-SHA256(secret, realm|method|intent|request|expires|digest|opaque)), recomputed and constant-time-compared on verification with no server-side store.

acceptance_criteria: OpenAPI 3.1.0-valid output
x-payment-info / x-service-info follow the latest discovery extension
Emits multi-offer `offers` array form; accepts single-offer shorthand on parse

Cross-check the generated document against mppx's OpenAPI output for an equivalent endpoint config. Complements (does not replace) `mix mpp.manifest`.

task.title: Tempo payment method (8 sub-tasks 13a-h)
task.body:
On-chain TIP-20 transfer verification via Tempo's JSON-RPC. Implements MPP.Methods.Tempo supporting both `type="hash"` (client-broadcast) and `type="transaction"` (server-broadcast) credential paths.

Shipped:
- TransferWithMemo support — memo matching for `transferWithMemo(address,uint256,bytes32)` calls, enforced per spec when `methodDetails.memo` is configured. Discovered via real Moderato receipts that the `memo` parameter is `indexed` (topic, not data field).
- Fee payer co-signing — server-side fee sponsorship for `feePayer: true` with 0x78 domain signing and call scope validation (whitelist of 4 allowed selector patterns matching mppx `callScopes`).
- Optimistic broadcast mode — `wait_for_confirmation: false` simulates payment call via `eth_call` then broadcasts asynchronously, returning an optimistic receipt without waiting for block inclusion.
- Transaction dedup store (MPP.Tempo.Store behaviour) — pluggable replay protection with get/1, put/2, and optional atomic check_and_mark/2 callbacks; different dedup semantics per credential path (hash: post-verification mark; transaction: pre-broadcast reservation).
- Built-in ConCacheStore (MPP.Tempo.ConCacheStore) — ETS-based dedup store with automatic TTL via ConCache.
- v-value normalization in recover_sender/2 (legacy 27/28 → recid 0/1) for ox/tempo SDK interop.
- ox/tempo cross-validation of 0x76 RLP encoding via QuickBEAM + esbuild bundle against the ox/tempo TypeScript SDK.
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.Methods.Tempo for on-chain TIP-20 transfer verification over Tempo's JSON-RPC, supporting both client-broadcast (type=hash) and server-broadcast (type=transaction) credential paths — including TransferWithMemo matching (indexed memo topic), fee-payer co-signing with 0x78 domain signing and call-scope validation, optimistic broadcast mode, a pluggable dedup store behaviour with a built-in ConCacheStore, v-value normalization in recover_sender/2, and ox/tempo cross-validation of 0x76 RLP encoding.

task.title: Extract onchain_tempo package
task.body:
Extracted Tempo chain primitives from mpp into the standalone `onchain_tempo` package; MPP now depends on `onchain_tempo` (Hex.pm) and delegates chain operations.

Moved out:
- `MPP.Tempo.Transaction` → `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction` (deserialize, payment matching, fee payer co-signing)
- `MPP.Test.TempoTxBuilder` → `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.Builder`
- TempoTestHelpers calldata fns → `Onchain.Tempo.TIP20`
- Broadcast fns → `Onchain.Tempo.RPC`
- `parse_transfer_with_memo_logs/1` → `Onchain.Tempo.Transfer`

Stayed in mpp:
- `MPP.Methods.Tempo` (verify/2, challenge_method_details/1, dedup store, Plug error wrapping)
- `MPP.Tempo.Store` behaviour + `MPP.Tempo.ConCacheStore` (payment-protocol replay protection)
- `simulate_payment_call` (MPP-specific eth_call simulation)

RPC adapter functions bridge onchain_tempo's `{:error, string}` to MPP's `{:error, Errors.t()}` RFC 9457 format.
task.implemented: Extracted Tempo chain primitives (Transaction, TIP20 calldata, RPC broadcast, transfer-log parsing, tx builder) out of mpp into the standalone onchain_tempo Hex package; MPP now depends on onchain_tempo and delegates chain operations, keeping the payment-protocol layer (MPP.Methods.Tempo, dedup store, simulate_payment_call) in mpp with RPC adapters bridging onchain_tempo error strings to RFC 9457 errors.

task.title: Bump onchain + onchain_tempo deps
task.body:
Bumped `{:onchain, "~> 0.4"}` → `~> 0.5` and `{:onchain_tempo, "~> 0.1"}` → `~> 0.1.1`. Full test suite and dialyzer passed unchanged — no code changes required in MPP.

Scope shrank: onchain_tempo shipped the coordinated dep bump as 0.1.1 (not 0.2.0 as originally anticipated), so no major-version migration was needed. Constraint tightened to `~> 0.1.1` to express the actual floor — onchain_tempo 0.1.1 requires `onchain ~> 0.5`, so the previous pair could have resolved to an inconsistent combination on a fresh install.
task.implemented: Bumped onchain ~> 0.4 → ~> 0.5 and onchain_tempo ~> 0.1 → ~> 0.1.1, tightening the constraint to express the actual floor — the full test suite and dialyzer passed unchanged with no code changes required in MPP.

task.title: Tempo integration tests → onchain_tempo.Faucet
task.body:
Bumped `{:onchain_tempo, "~> 0.1.1"}` → `~> 0.2`. Deleted the hand-rolled `defp fund_test_address/2` (custom `tempo_fundAddress` JSON-RPC wrapper) and replaced every call site with `defp fresh_wallet!/1` delegating to `Onchain.Tempo.Faucet.fresh_funded_wallet/1`.

Removed hardcoded `@sender_key` / `@fee_payer_key` module attrs — each broadcasting test now mints a fresh, funded keypair per test. Dropped the `__MODULE__.NonceAgent` shared counter (per-test fresh wallets start at nonce 0). `setup_all` now mints one fixture wallet to seed shared tx_hash fixtures, then returns.

Per-test fresh wallet (not per-session) removes the nonce-race coupling so a future move to `async: true` is safe. Inline `fresh_wallet!/1` calls (not a global setup block) avoid wasting Moderato faucet calls on the ~7 tests that only use fixture hashes.
task.implemented: Migrated the Tempo integration tests to Onchain.Tempo.Faucet (bumping onchain_tempo to ~> 0.2), replacing the hand-rolled fund_test_address/2 with a fresh_wallet!/1 helper that mints a fresh, funded keypair per broadcasting test — removing hardcoded sender/fee-payer keys and the shared NonceAgent counter so a future move to async: true is safe.

task.title: Generic EVM method
task.body:
On-chain payment verification for any EVM chain (Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, etc.). `MPP.Methods.EVM` implements the `MPP.Method` behaviour.

- Hash-only credential path: client broadcasts tx, sends hash, server verifies receipt.
- ERC-20 transfers verified via Transfer event log parsing (`Onchain.Transfer.parse_logs/1`).
- Native ETH transfers verified via transaction value + recipient matching.
- Currency convention: ERC-20 tokens use contract address; native ETH uses "ETH" or zero address.
- Sepolia integration tests added: ERC-20 via WETH (wraps ETH → deposit() → transfer), native ETH, error cases, full 402 flow.

Hash-only verification (no signed-tx broadcast path) — simpler, universally works across all EVM chains without chain-specific transaction types. RPC calls via Req directly (Onchain.RPC uses Signet → Finch and bypasses Req entirely; Req enables Req.Test stubbing).
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.Methods.EVM implementing on-chain payment verification for any EVM chain via a hash-only credential path — ERC-20 transfers verified through Transfer event log parsing and native ETH via transaction value/recipient matching, with RPC calls over Req (for Req.Test stubbing) and Sepolia integration tests covering ERC-20 (WETH), native ETH, error cases, and the full 402 flow.

Interactive demo server for exploring the 402 payment flow without real payment credentials.

- `MPP.Demo.Method` — toy payment method accepting `"demo-token"` as magic payload

task.title: Live protocol integration tests
task.body:
Read-only integration tests against the live `mpp.dev/api/ping/paid` endpoint, validating protocol compatibility with the reference MPP server. Verifies client-side parsing against a real 402 Tempo challenge: 402 response structure, challenge parsing, field validation, charge request decoding, RFC 9457 error body format, and challengeId cross-validation between body and header.

Read-only only (no wallet/payment required). Each test fetches a fresh 402 to avoid challenge expiration. Validates protocol invariants rather than deployment-specific values.
task.implemented: Shipped read-only live integration tests against the mpp.dev/api/ping/paid endpoint that validate client-side protocol compatibility with the reference MPP server — checking 402 structure, challenge parsing, field validation, charge-request decoding, RFC 9457 error bodies, and challengeId cross-validation, with each test fetching a fresh 402 to avoid expiration.

task.title: Multi-challenge parsing
task.body:
Added `MPP.Headers.parse_challenges/1` for parsing `WWW-Authenticate` headers containing multiple `Payment` challenges. Splits on scheme boundaries, returns `{:ok, [Challenge.t()]}` for successfully parsed Payment challenges. Partial-failure tolerance matches mppx `deserializeList` semantics.

Boundary detection (not comma splitting) — commas inside quoted auth-param values are not splitters. `valid_scheme_start?` validates that a scheme match is at position 0 or preceded by a comma, preventing false matches inside quoted strings like `description="Payment plan"`. Returns `:no_payment_challenges` error when no Payment schemes are found.

Unblocked Task 33b (HTTP client transport).
task.implemented: Added MPP.Headers.parse_challenges/1, parsing WWW-Authenticate headers carrying multiple Payment challenges by scheme-boundary detection (not comma splitting, so commas in quoted auth-params don't split), with partial-failure tolerance matching mppx deserializeList and a :no_payment_challenges error when none are found.

task.title: Body digest
task.body:
`MPP.BodyDigest` — SHA-256 body digest computation and verification for request body binding.

- `compute/1` hashes string or map body, returns `"sha-256=<base64>"` (standard base64, no padding — matches mppx)
- `verify/2` does constant-time comparison via `Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2`
- Maps are JSON-encoded before hashing
- Registered in `MPP.describe(:body_digest)` via Discoverable
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.BodyDigest for SHA-256 request-body binding — compute/1 hashes a string or JSON-encoded map into "sha-256=<base64>" (unpadded, mppx-compatible) and verify/2 does constant-time comparison via Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2, registered for discovery via MPP.describe(:body_digest).

task.title: Amount and decimals helpers
task.body:
`MPP.Amount` — pure integer/string arithmetic for converting human-readable amounts to base units.

- `parse_units/2` — "1.5" + 6 decimals → "1500000" (cross-validated against mpp-rs test vectors)
- `with_base_units/2` — applies parse_units to any intent struct's amount field
- `parse_dollar_amount/2` — "$1.50" + decimals → `{"150", "usd", 2}` with currency symbol detection ($, €, £, ¥) and suffix codes ("1.50 USD")

Caller supplies decimals explicitly (no currency-to-decimals inference) — matches mppx and mpp-rs design. Zero allowed (zero-amount charges valid for identity/proof flows). No floating point anywhere — all arithmetic via string splitting and padding.

BREAKING in v0.4.0: `parse_dollar_amount/1` → `parse_dollar_amount/2` (caller supplies decimals explicitly). Implicit inference created correctness risks (HUF/TWD classification is debatable) and diverged from spec's "explicit configuration" philosophy.
task.implemented: Shipped MPP.Amount for pure integer/string base-unit conversion with no floating point — parse_units/2 (cross-validated against mpp-rs vectors), with_base_units/2 over intent structs, and parse_dollar_amount/2 with currency-symbol/suffix detection; caller supplies decimals explicitly (BREAKING in v0.4.0: parse_dollar_amount/1 → /2).

task.title: Expiration and DID helpers
acceptance_criteria: MPP.Expires.minutes(5) returns valid ISO 8601 ~5 minutes from now
MPP.Expires.months(1) returns ~30 days from now (mppx-compatible)
MPP.Expires.assert!/1 raises on expired/nil/malformed timestamps
MPP.Expires.assert!/2 accepts optional challenge_id for error context
MPP.DID.evm_did/2 returns correctly formatted DID string
Unit tests for each helper
task.body: Add `MPP.Expires` module with `seconds/1`, `minutes/1`, `hours/1`, `days/1`, `weeks/1`, `months/1` (= n × 30 × 86400s, matching mppx convention), `years/1` returning ISO 8601 datetime strings offset from `DateTime.utc_now/0`. Add `assert!/1` that raises on nil, malformed, or expired timestamps (timezone-aware comparison, malformed ISO edge cases), plus `assert!/2` overload taking an optional `challenge_id` for richer error context. Add `MPP.DID` module with `evm_did/2` that takes an address and chain_id and returns `"did:pkh:eip155:<chain_id>:<address>"`.

task.title: Verifier extraction + JCS
task.body:
Extracted the verification pipeline from `MPP.Plug` into a transport-neutral `MPP.Verifier` module. Added `MPP.JCS` for RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme.

- `MPP.JCS` — RFC 8785 canonical JSON (MPP subset: ASCII keys, string/integer/boolean/nil values). Floats rejected with FunctionClauseError. Matches mppx/mpp-rs output for all MPP protocol data.
- `MPP.Verifier` — transport-neutral `verify/2` with the full verification pipeline: HMAC challenge binding, realm match, expiration, request match, method.verify. No Plug dependency.
- `MPP.Plug` refactored to a thin HTTP adapter delegating to `MPP.Verifier`.
- MCP `encode_request` updated from `Jason.encode!` to `JCS.canonicalize` (cross-SDK HMAC interop).

Verifier accepts keyword opts (`:secret_key`, `:realm`, `:method`, `:charge`, `:method_config`) rather than Plug types — zero coupling to HTTP transport. Always returns `{:ok, Receipt.t()} | {:error, Errors.t()}` with structured errors. JCS implemented inline (~30 lines) rather than adding a dependency. Dropped the `:request_serializer` option — JCS is mandatory per spec, not configurable.

Unblocked Tasks 32b (MCP server transport) and 33b (HTTP client transport).
task.implemented: Extracted the verification pipeline from MPP.Plug into a transport-neutral MPP.Verifier (verify/2 over keyword opts, returning {:ok, Receipt.t()} | {:error, Errors.t()}) and added MPP.JCS for RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization (MPP subset, floats rejected) — refactoring MPP.Plug into a thin HTTP adapter and switching MCP encode_request to JCS for cross-SDK HMAC interop.

task.title: Generic dedup at Plug level
acceptance_criteria: Optional :store option in MPP.Plug config (shared across methods)
Dedup check before method.verify/2, mark after success
Tempo skips plug-level dedup when it has its own store configured
EVM and Stripe benefit from replay protection when store is configured
Unit test: same credential rejected on second use
Backward compatible — no store = current behavior (no dedup)
task.body: Lift replay protection from Tempo-only to all payment methods. Currently `MPP.Tempo.Store` provides dedup for Tempo credentials, but EVM and Stripe accept the same payment proof twice within the challenge window. Add optional `:store` to `MPP.Plug.Config` (shared across all methods). Before calling `method.verify/2`, check if the credential has been seen (keyed on challenge_id + payload hash). After successful verification, mark as used. Methods that already have their own dedup (Tempo) can skip the plug-level check. The `MPP.Tempo.Store` behaviour is already the right interface — reuse it at the Plug level.

task.title: Accept-Payment header support
acceptance_criteria: parse_accept_payment/1 handles q-values, wildcards (tempo/*, */session), and malformed input (returns empty list per spec MAY-ignore)
format_accept_payment/1 builds header from [{method, intent, q}]
MPP.Plug filters challenges when Accept-Payment present (q=0 skips)
Client-side `MPP.Client.AcceptPolicy` honoring server-advertised methods (parallels mpp-rs AcceptPaymentPolicy)
Unit tests: wildcard matching, q-value ordering, malformed input
Descripex annotations
task.body: Add `MPP.Headers.parse_accept_payment/1` parsing spec §7.4 `Accept-Payment` into a ranked `[{method, intent, q}]` list. Add `format_accept_payment/1` for client-side generation. Update `MPP.Plug` to filter/reorder `WWW-Authenticate` challenges based on client's `Accept-Payment` (no-op when absent, per spec). Update `MPP.Client.Transport.HTTP` (Task 33b) to optionally set `Accept-Payment` from a provider list. Add a client-side `MPP.Client.AcceptPolicy` that honors server-advertised methods on the response path — parallel to mpp-rs `AcceptPaymentPolicy` (read `refs/mpp-rs/src/client/accept_payment_policy.rs` at pickup time to confirm policy shape and filter/order semantics).

task.title: Session error types
task.body:
Extended `MPP.Errors` with 8 new RFC 9457 problem types, cross-validated against mppx `Errors.ts`.

- 7 session error types under `session/` URI prefix: `:insufficient_balance`, `:invalid_signature`, `:signer_mismatch`, `:amount_exceeds_deposit`, `:delta_too_small`, `:channel_not_found` (410), `:channel_closed` (410)
- 1 core error type: `:payment_action_required` for 3DS flows (402)

Channel errors use HTTP 410 Gone (not 402) matching mppx. `:channel_closed` maps to URI suffix `session/channel-finalized` (matching mppx's `ChannelClosedError` which uses the "finalized" term in the URI).
task.implemented: Extended MPP.Errors with 8 new RFC 9457 problem types cross-validated against mppx Errors.ts — 7 session error types under the session/ URI prefix (channel errors using HTTP 410 Gone) plus a core :payment_action_required (402) for 3DS flows.

task.title: Session intent schema
acceptance_criteria: MPP.Intents.Session struct with all fields
new/1 validates required fields, returns {:ok, session} or {:error, reason}
Serializes to same JSON shape as mpp-rs SessionRequest
Descripex annotations
MPP.Method behaviour updated to support intent: "session" alongside "charge"
task.body: Add `MPP.Intents.Session` as the session intent request schema, parallel to `MPP.Intents.Charge`. Fields: `amount` (required, per-unit rate in base units), `unit_type` (optional, e.g. "second", "minute", "request"), `currency` (required), `recipient` (optional), `suggested_deposit` (optional), `decimals` (optional, transient), `external_id` (optional string, per mpp-rs `SessionRequest`), `method_details` (optional map). Validate with same pattern as `Charge` — struct with `new/1` validation, `to_request/1` and `from_request/1` serialization.

task.title: Tempo SessionReceipt
task.body:
Added `MPP.Methods.Tempo.SessionReceipt` — session-intent receipt type paralleling `MPP.Receipt` (charge-intent).

- `new/1` sets method/intent/status defaults, auto-fills timestamp, defaults `reference` to `channel_id`.
- `to_header/1` / `from_header/1` follow the base64url-JSON pattern with camelCase wire keys (`challengeId`, `channelId`, `acceptedCumulative`, `txHash`). Optional `units` / `tx_hash` omitted when nil rather than serialized as `null`.
- `from_header/1` returns `{:error, :invalid_base64 | :invalid_json | :missing_required_fields}` on malformed input.
- Cross-validated against `refs/mpp-rs/src/protocol/methods/tempo/session_receipt.rs` test vectors and `refs/mppx/src/tempo/session/Receipt.ts` wire format.
- Descripex annotations under `/methods/tempo` namespace.

Function names `to_header`/`from_header` diverge from `MPP.Receipt`'s `encode`/`decode` — session receipts have no other entry points, so header-oriented naming is clearer. `MPP.Headers` helpers left untouched (typed to `Receipt.t()`); revisit when Task 31 wires session receipts into the Plug response path.
task.implemented: Added MPP.Methods.Tempo.SessionReceipt — a session-intent receipt type paralleling MPP.Receipt with new/1 defaulting, to_header/1 and from_header/1 following the base64url-JSON pattern with camelCase wire keys (omitting nil optionals) and typed error returns, cross-validated against mpp-rs and mppx vectors with Descripex annotations.

task.title: Channel state and voucher types
acceptance_criteria: Channel ID computation matches mppx/mpp-rs for same inputs
EIP-712 voucher signature verification
Channel state transitions: open → active → closed
Store behaviour with ETS-backed default implementation
Cross-validated channel IDs against mppx Channel.ts
task.body:
Add `MPP.Session.Channel` for channel state management and `MPP.Session.Voucher` for EIP-712 typed voucher verification. Channel state: channel_id, payer, recipient, token, deposit, cumulative_amount, status. Channel ID = `keccak256(abi.encode(payer, payee, token, salt, authorizedSigner, escrowContract, chainId))`. Voucher: channel_id, cumulative_amount, signature. Channel store behaviour (`MPP.Session.Store`) for pluggable persistence. Action values are camelCase in JSON (`"open"` / `"topUp"` / `"voucher"` / `"close"`); use snake_case only for Elixir atoms.

Note 2026-06-12: mpp-rs landed TIP-1034 session client primitives including precompile-backed voucher support (#288, commit 0d57f96) — the production-path successor to the contract-backed v1 channel. At pickup, read `refs/mpp-rs/src/protocol/methods/tempo/precompile_voucher.rs` and `refs/mpp-rs/src/client/tempo/session/` to decide whether to model v1 (contract) and v2 (precompile) voucher types together or stage v2 as a follow-up.

task.title: Session credential actions
acceptance_criteria: Four action handlers: open, voucher, topUp, close
Correct payload schema per action (JSON: "open" / "voucher" / "topUp" / "close"; Elixir atoms snake_case)
Plug integration for session endpoints
Balance tracking per channel
Unit tests for each action lifecycle
task.body: Implement the four session credential actions: `open` (client deposits, opens channel), `voucher` (client presents signed cumulative-amount voucher for ongoing access), `topUp` (client adds deposit to existing channel), `close` (either party closes channel). Each action maps to a credential payload shape. Server dispatches to correct action handler based on `credential.payload.action`. Integrate with `MPP.Plug` so session endpoints work alongside charge endpoints.

task.title: MCP types and constants
task.body:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) transport helpers for embedding MPP payment flows in JSON-RPC messages.

- `MPP.Mcp` module with 4 spec constants (`-32042`, `-32043`, `org.paymentauth/credential`, `org.paymentauth/receipt`).
- Server helpers: `extract_credential/1`, `payment_required_error/1`, `verification_failed_error/2`, `attach_receipt/3`.
- Client helpers: `payment_required?/1`, `extract_challenges/1`, `attach_credential/2`.
- Full round-trip test: challenge → error → extract → credential → attach → receipt.

Single `MPP.Mcp` module (matches mpp-rs single `mcp.rs` pattern). No new structs — reuses existing Challenge/Credential/Receipt; MCP-specific shapes are plain maps matching JSON-RPC wire format. MCP credentials are plain JSON maps in `_meta` (not base64url-encoded like HTTP transport).

Codex review fixes (v0.4.0):
- Crash on non-map/non-binary request (`encode_request/1` catch-all returning `:invalid` sentinel, checked in `challenge_from_map`).
- Optional fields type-validated (`validate_optional_strings/1` rejects non-binary `description`, `digest`, `expires`, `opaque`).
- Inaccurate public specs corrected on `extract_credential/1` and `extract_challenges/1`.
- `MPP.Mcp` added to Discoverable registry; `MPP.describe(:mcp)` now works.
- MCP `request` field format — decoded base64url→JSON on output, re-encoded JSON→base64url on input (internal Challenge.request stays base64url for HMAC binding).
- Defensive `challenge_from_map` returns `{:error, :invalid_challenge}` instead of raising on malformed input.

Known limitation: `encode_request` uses `Jason.encode!/1` for the native JSON → base64url path. Safe for same-server round-trips; cross-implementation interop depends on Task 34's JCS (now resolved in v0.4.0 as a follow-up).
task.implemented: Shipped the MPP.Mcp module with MCP/JSON-RPC transport helpers — the 4 spec constants plus server-side (extract_credential, payment_required_error, verification_failed_error, attach_receipt) and client-side (payment_required?, extract_challenges, attach_credential) helpers reusing existing Challenge/Credential/Receipt types, with full round-trip tests and Codex-review hardening for malformed input.

task.title: MCP server transport
acceptance_criteria: Server-side MCP transport/adapter for JSON-RPC handler inputs and outputs
Reads credentials from request _meta
Emits payment-required errors with challenges and RFC 9457 problem details
Attaches receipts to successful result _meta
Unit tests with mock MCP handler exchanges
task.body: Add a server-side MCP transport/adapter that bridges the transport-neutral verifier into JSON-RPC handler environments. Mirror the reference SDK behavior: read credentials from `_meta["org.paymentauth/credential"]`, emit payment-required errors with code `-32042` and challenge data, and attach receipts into `_meta["org.paymentauth/receipt"]` on successful responses. This turns Phase 11 from a types/helpers layer into an actually mountable MCP server integration.

task.title: Client PaymentProvider behaviour
task.body:
Client-side counterpart to server-side `MPP.Method` — where methods *verify* payment proof, providers *create* it.

- `MPP.Client.PaymentProvider` behaviour with `supports?/3` and `pay/2` callbacks.
- `MPP.Client.MultiProvider` struct wrapping `[{module, config}]` tuples with first-match dispatch.
- Convenience functions on `PaymentProvider` for direct module delegation.
- Descripex annotations on both modules, registered in `MPP.describe/0-2`.

Config is explicit on every callback (no global state) — matches library design principle and enables multi-tenant usage. `MultiProvider` is a concrete struct, not a behaviour implementation — avoids awkward arity clashes. Provider ordering matters: first `supports?/3` match wins (mirrors mpp-rs `MultiProvider` semantics). Error atom `:unsupported_payment_method` when no provider matches.
task.implemented: Shipped the client-side MPP.Client.PaymentProvider behaviour (supports?/3, pay/2) — the create-payment counterpart to the server-side verify-payment MPP.Method — plus an MPP.Client.MultiProvider struct wrapping {module, config} tuples with first-match dispatch, explicit per-callback config (no global state), and Descripex annotations.

task.title: HTTP client transport
task.body:
Added `MPP.Client.Transport` behaviour with three callbacks (`payment_required?/1`, `get_challenges/1`, `set_credential/2`) — transport-agnostic so Task 33d (MCP) implements the same shape.

Added `MPP.Client.Transport.HTTP` implementing the behaviour over `Req.Request` / `Req.Response`. Joins repeated `WWW-Authenticate` values before delegating to `MPP.Headers.parse_challenges/1`. Attaches credentials via `MPP.Headers.format_credential/1` (`Authorization: Payment <base64url>`).

Added `MPP.Client.Transport.select_challenge/2` — a small pure helper (not a callback) that picks the first challenge supported by a `MultiProvider`, matching mpp-rs's "first-supported-in-offer-order" baseline. Ranking via `Accept-Payment` (Task 37) will wrap this later.

`set_credential/2` takes a decoded `MPP.Credential.t()` rather than a formatted string — each transport owns its wire format. `select_challenge/2` lives on the behaviour module so Tasks 33c and 33d can reuse it without duplicating the `Enum.find`. No Req client construction in the transport — callers pass in `Req.Request`/`Req.Response` structs.
task.implemented: Added the transport-agnostic MPP.Client.Transport behaviour (payment_required?/1, get_challenges/1, set_credential/2) and its HTTP implementation over Req.Request/Req.Response — joining repeated WWW-Authenticate values before parse_challenges/1 and attaching credentials as Authorization: Payment <base64url> — plus a pure select_challenge/2 helper picking the first MultiProvider-supported challenge in offer order.

task.title: Payment-aware Req plugin
acceptance_criteria: Req plugin with attach/2 for pipeline integration
Automatic 402 detection and retry
Provider selection from multi-challenge responses
Non-402 passthrough
Integration test against mix mpp.demo server
task.body: Add `MPP.Client.Req` as a Req plugin that intercepts 402 responses, extracts the challenge, calls the configured provider's `pay/1`, and retries with the credential. Pattern: `Req.new() |> MPP.Client.Req.attach(provider: my_provider)`. Non-402 responses pass through untouched. This is the Elixir equivalent of mpp-rs `PaymentExt` for reqwest and mppx `Fetch.from()`.

task.title: MCP client transport
acceptance_criteria: Implements Transport behaviour for JSON-RPC messages
Uses MPP.Mcp constants and types
Handles payment-required error detection
Credential attachment to request params
Approval-callback hook invoked before paying (parallels mppx #522 McpClient approval callbacks; read refs/mppx/src/mcp-sdk/client/McpClient.ts at pickup)
Unit tests with mock JSON-RPC exchanges
task.body: Add `MPP.Client.Transport.MCP` implementing the Transport behaviour for JSON-RPC messages. `payment_required?/1` checks error code -32042. `get_challenges/1` extracts from `error.data.challenges`. `set_credential/2` inserts into `params._meta["org.paymentauth/credential"]`. Uses types from Task 32 (`MPP.Mcp`).

task.title: Built-in charge providers
acceptance_criteria: Built-in Tempo charge provider implementing PaymentProvider
Built-in Stripe charge provider implementing PaymentProvider
Public API/docs show end-to-end client usage with the Req plugin or transport layer
One integration path per provider against a real or protocol-faithful challenge flow
Provider selection works cleanly through MPP.Client.MultiProvider
task.body: Add built-in client providers so the SDK is useful without every consumer writing their own provider first. Ship `MPP.Client.Providers.Tempo` and `MPP.Client.Providers.Stripe` for charge intent, mirroring the concrete client offerings in the reference SDKs. Each provider should parse the challenge request, execute payment with explicit config, and return a credential for the generic transport/plugin layer. Session-capable providers can layer on after Phase 10 lands.

task.title: Lightning charge method
acceptance_criteria: Implements MPP.Method behaviour
challenge_method_details/1 returns invoice, paymentHash, network
verify/2 checks SHA256(preimage) == paymentHash
Unit tests with known preimage/hash pairs
Integration test with regtest Lightning node (if available)
task.body: Implement `MPP.Methods.Lightning` for charge intent. Server generates a BOLT11 invoice per request, issues 402 with invoice + payment hash. Client pays via Lightning Network, receives preimage on HTLC settlement, retries with preimage as credential. Server verifies SHA256(preimage) == stored payment_hash. Challenge details include invoice string, paymentHash (hex), network (mainnet/regtest/signet), amount in satoshis. Credential payload: `preimage` (32-byte lowercase hex). Requires Lightning node client library (external dep TBD — LND gRPC or similar).

task.title: Lightning session method
acceptance_criteria: Session lifecycle: open → bearer → topUp → close
Per-unit metering with balance tracking
SSE "need-topup" event emission
Refund via return invoice on close
Session store behaviour (pluggable: ETS, database, etc.)
task.body: Implement prepaid streaming sessions for metered payments (e.g., LLM token generation). Client opens session by paying deposit invoice, provides return invoice for refunds. Server deducts per-unit cost from balance during streaming, emits SSE "need-topup" when balance low. Client can topUp with new deposit or close session (server refunds unspent balance via return invoice). Stateful — needs session store (unlike all other methods). Credential actions: open, bearer, topUp, close (Lightning uses preimage-as-bearer-token, not Tempo's cumulative-voucher model — see `draft-lightning-session-00.md`). Defer until charge method proven and demand exists.

task.title: Solana charge method
acceptance_criteria: Implements MPP.Method behaviour
Pull mode: verify signed tx bytes, broadcast, confirm
Push mode: verify confirmed signature via RPC
SOL native + SPL token support
Fee payer co-signing
Payment splits (up to 8 recipients)
Unit tests with mocked Solana RPC responses
task.body: Implement `MPP.Methods.Solana` for charge intent. Pull mode: client signs Solana transfer tx, sends signed bytes in credential; server optionally co-signs (fee payer), broadcasts, waits for confirmation. Push mode: client broadcasts tx, sends confirmed signature; server fetches tx from RPC and verifies payment details (amount, recipient, token). Challenge details include recipient (base58 pubkey), amount (lamports or token base units), currency ("sol" or mint address), network, decimals, tokenProgram, feePayer flag, feePayerKey, optional splits array. Requires Solana RPC client (external dep TBD).

task.title: Card charge method
acceptance_criteria: Implements MPP.Method behaviour
RSA key pair generation and JWKS endpoint support
JWE token decryption (RSA-OAEP-256 + AES-256-GCM)
Network token validation (PAN, expiry, network)
Server Enabler integration pattern
Unit tests with crafted JWE tokens
task.body: Implement `MPP.Methods.Card` for charge intent. Client works with a Client Enabler to provision an encrypted network token from a token service provider. Token is encrypted with server's RSA public key via JWE (RSA-OAEP-256 + AES-256-GCM). Credential includes encrypted payload, card network (visa/mastercard/amex/discover), PAN last four, expiration, optional cardholder name and billing address, optional PAR. Server forwards encrypted credential to Server Enabler for decryption and processing. Challenge details include accepted networks, merchant name, encryption key (JWK or JWKS URI). Requires RSA key management and JWE library. Defer until ecosystem demand.

task.title: Stellar charge method
task.body: Implement `MPP.Methods.Stellar` for charge intent (`refs/mpp-specs/specs/methods/stellar/draft-stellar-charge-00.md`). Pull mode (client signs XDR, server submits) + push mode (hash). SEP-41 token verification via Soroban RPC `getTransaction`. Add `settlement-failed` error code to `MPP.Errors`. Neither mppx nor mpp-rs implement Stellar yet.

task.title: EVM Permit2 credential path
task.body: Implement RECOMMENDED Permit2 credential type per `draft-evm-charge-00.md:392-495`. Client signs EIP-712 Permit2 authorization; server submits via Permit2 contract. Enables gas sponsorship and atomic split-payments.

task.title: EVM EIP-3009 authorization credential
task.body: Implement `authorization` credential type per `draft-evm-charge-00.md:592-645` for USDC/EURC `transferWithAuthorization`. Use `challengeHash` as EIP-3009 nonce for replay protection.

task.title: Tier-2 pinned-field verification
acceptance_criteria: All fields the spec / reference impl require to pin are pinned
Pinning mismatch returns a distinct error (vs. HMAC mismatch)
Cross-validated against mpp-rs test vectors for both pass and fail paths
Unit + property tests for field-by-field divergence
task.body:
Extend `MPP.Verifier` with explicit field-by-field pinning of the credential's echoed challenge against the live request — re-asserting realm, method, request, expires, and digest agree. Catches cross-realm or replayed-with-different-request attacks that HMAC alone validates because the HMAC happens to match.

Read the current Tier-2 pattern in `refs/mpp-rs` (server-side charge path) at implementation time — the latest reference impl defines which fields must pin and how to surface mismatch errors. Match its semantics; let the Elixir shape follow `MPP.Verifier` conventions. Distinguish the pinning-mismatch error from the HMAC-mismatch error so callers can tell replay-attacks from corrupt credentials.

task.title: Tempo + session hardening audit vs. latest reference impls
acceptance_criteria: Delta report listing each upstream fix vs. our equivalent (parity / partial / missing)
Targeted patches for missing fixes
Integration tests against Moderato testnet for each newly covered case
No regression in existing Tempo / session integration tests
task.body:
Audit `MPP.Methods.Tempo`, the `MPP.Tempo.*` modules, and (when Phase 10 lands) session billing against the latest Tempo + session-channel hardening in mppx and mpp-rs. Read `refs/mppx` and `refs/mpp-rs` git logs + relevant src/ at pickup time to identify which fixes are not yet reflected in our Elixir impl.

Likely areas (illustrative — confirm against latest refs at pickup): challenge-bound memo validation on pull transactions, raw-opaque byte-exact preservation through round-trip, expired-challenge rejection on both server and client, fee-payer sponsorship hardening, post-channel-close charge rejection, session-channel scoping to the active challenge, replayed-voucher rejection, fresh-deposit state preservation, broadcast-transaction memo validation, channel-locking during close, fee-payer approve-target validation, proof-signature-to-wallet binding.

Produce a delta report (parity / partial / missing per upstream fix), then patch the gaps with targeted commits. Integration tests against Moderato testnet (and Phase 10 session vectors where applicable) for each newly covered case.

Concrete upstream deltas found 2026-06-12 (confirm still-current at pickup): externalId explicitly added to PaymentWitness (mpp-specs #266 — verify our `MPP.Methods.Tempo.SessionReceipt` wire format includes it); fee-payer token allowlist (mpp-rs #286); client-side Tempo chain pinning (mpp-rs 8880cf7 — overlaps Task 45); `Store::put_if_absent` atomic-CAS semantics vs our `check_and_mark` (mpp-rs #280 — confirm our ConCacheStore atomicity matches); Stripe charge externalId binding fix (mppx #537 — also touches `MPP.Methods.Stripe`); hosted Tempo fee-payer fills (mppx #538).

task.title: Client challenge ordering hook
acceptance_criteria: Configurable ordering callback on the HTTP transport
Default behavior unchanged (server-advertised order)
Multi-provider dispatch honors the reordered list
Unit tests covering: identity, reverse, filter-then-reorder, empty
task.body: When a server returns a multi-method 402, our client should let the consumer reorder the offered challenges before selection (e.g. prefer known/cheap methods first). Read the current hook surface in `refs/mppx/src/client/Mppx.ts` at pickup time to confirm the contract shape. Implement as a configurable callback on `MPP.Client.Transport.HTTP` (and the multi-provider dispatch path) — defaulting to server order if no callback is provided.

task.title: WebSocket transport binding
acceptance_criteria: Server-side WS adapter for JSON-RPC + payment challenges
Client-side `MPP.Client.Transport` impl for WS
Payment-required detection and credential attachment match reference framing
Retry/backoff posture matches upstream (no amplification)
Integration test against a stub or real WS endpoint
task.body:
Implement MPP over WebSocket — server adapter for JSON-RPC carried over WS with payment challenges riding on subscription handshakes, and a client-side `MPP.Client.Transport` impl for WS. Read the current WS transport in `refs/mpp-rs` (server-side WS handler and the `alloy-transport-mpp` crate) at implementation time to confirm framing, error codes, challenge placement, and retry/backoff semantics (upstream has hardened against retry amplification — match that posture).

Integrate cleanly with the existing `MPP.Client.Transport` behaviour from Task 33b. The server adapter should be transport-agnostic w.r.t. the underlying WS library (consumers bring their own — Cowboy, Bandit, etc.).

task.title: JSON-RPC transport (non-MCP)
acceptance_criteria: JSON-RPC request/response with payment challenges on the same channel
Error code shape matches spec + reference impls
Client-side `MPP.Client.Transport` impl
Server-side adapter usable from Plug
task.body:
Bare JSON-RPC transport binding (non-MCP-framed) per the spec's transport section. Most consumers reach for MCP — this is for spec completeness and the rare consumer that wants JSON-RPC without MCP's tool/meta layer. Defer-tier; pull forward when first downstream asks.

At pickup time, read the bare-JSON-RPC transport adapters in `refs/mpp-rs` and `refs/mppx` (the non-MCP paths) plus the spec's transport section at `paymentauth.org` to confirm error codes and challenge placement.

task.title: Tempo subscriptions
acceptance_criteria: Subscription intent / receipt types
wallet_authorizeAccessKey integration matches reference impl
Fee-payer sponsored subscription path
Integration test against Moderato testnet
task.body: Defer-tier. Extend Phase 10 session work with Tempo subscription mode (recurring access-key authorization beyond single-channel session billing). Read `refs/mppx` Tempo subscription PRs and supporting `wallet_authorizeAccessKey` shape at pickup time to confirm the wire format and fee-payer integration. Pull forward only when a downstream consumer needs recurring payments — until then this stays low-Eff in the queue.

task.title: Hedera charge method
acceptance_criteria: MPP.Methods.Hedera implementing Method behaviour
Charge intent verification against Hedera network
Integration test against Hedera testnet
task.body: Defer-tier. Implement Hedera as the 8th charge method per `paymentauth.org` + `refs/mpp-specs/specs/methods/hedera/draft-hedera-charge-*.md`. No reference-impl integration upstream yet — when picked up, cross-check against whichever SDK has added it (mppx / mpp-rs / pympp / mpp-go) at that point. Pull forward only when first consumer asks.

task.title: Stripe Connect settlement options
acceptance_criteria: Challenge `method_details` carries Connect settlement fields per the latest discovery + Stripe method spec
Charge verification honors Connect routing (destination charge / direct charge / application fee)
Cross-validated against mppx's Stripe Connect output for an equivalent config
Integration test against Stripe test API using a Connect account
task.body: Extend `MPP.Methods.Stripe` with Stripe Connect settlement options (destination charge / direct charge / application fee routing). Read `paymentauth.org` Stripe charge spec + `refs/mpp-specs/specs/methods/stripe/` + the latest Stripe Connect handling in `refs/mppx` (search for `connect` / `settlement` in `src/methods/stripe/`) at implementation time — the spec and reference impl define which fields land in `methodDetails` and how the server routes the resulting PaymentIntent. Wire the `method_config` knobs for server-side Connect credentials separately from public `method_details`.

task.title: Payment event hooks (server-side observability surface)
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry events emitted at challenge / verify-start / verify-ok / verify-fail / receipt boundaries
Event shape carries enough context for metrics + tracing without leaking credentials
Event names + payload keys follow Elixir telemetry conventions (`[:mpp, :challenge | :verify | :receipt]`)
Cross-checked against the latest payment-event-hooks surface in reference SDKs
Unit test asserts each event fires exactly once on the happy and sad paths
task.body: Add a server-side observability surface — payment event hooks consumers can attach to for metrics, logging, and tracing. Read `refs/mpp-rs` (the payment event hooks extension) + the latest mppx event surface at pickup time to confirm which boundaries warrant events and what context they carry; mirror those semantics on top of standard Elixir `:telemetry`. Events must be safe to log — no raw credentials in payloads, only IDs and high-level outcomes. This is purely additive; no behavior change on the verify path.

task.title: Tempo store key prefixes (multi-tenant dedup)
acceptance_criteria: `MPP.Tempo.Store` behaviour (and `ConCacheStore` impl) accept a configurable key prefix
Default behavior unchanged when no prefix configured
Cross-tenant key collisions impossible when prefixes differ
Unit test: same tx hash under two prefixes treated as independent
task.body: Multi-tenant ergonomics for the Tempo dedup store — let consumers namespace dedup keys with a configurable prefix so two endpoints sharing a single store don't collide on identical tx hashes. Read the latest mppx Tempo store key-prefix pattern in `refs/mppx` (look in the proxy/tempo store code) at pickup time. Wire prefix through `MPP.Tempo.Store` behaviour and `MPP.Tempo.ConCacheStore` impl; default is no prefix (backward compatible).

task.title: Hash credential type audit + spec backfill
acceptance_criteria: Audit confirms whether `MPP.Credential` already supports the `hash` credential type per latest spec
If missing: parse / serialize / verify path for `hash` credentials added
Cross-validated against mppx + mpp-rs `hash` credential test vectors
Negative tests cover malformed and method-incompatible hash credentials
task.body: Audit our `MPP.Credential` against the latest spec at `paymentauth.org` (and `refs/mpp-specs/specs/`) for the `hash` credential type — the spec recently backfilled this as a first-class type alongside `transaction` / `bearer` / `signature`. Cross-check against the latest mppx and mpp-rs hash-credential handling. If our impl already covers it, the audit closes with a "parity confirmed" note; if not, add the parse / serialize / verify path.

task.title: GitHub Actions CI workflow
acceptance_criteria: Green workflow run on push/PR to development and main
Runs format-check, warnings-as-errors compile, non-integration tests, credo strict, dialyzer, sobelow, doctor
Dependency and PLT caching keyed on mix.lock
Integration-tagged tests excluded by default
out_of_scope: Integration tests requiring live credentials in CI
task.body: Add a GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml running the project's check stack on push and PR to development and main: mix format --check-formatted, compile with --warnings-as-errors, mix test.json excluding :integration, credo --strict, dialyzer (with cached PLTs), sobelow, and doctor. Cache deps, _build, and the dialyzer PLTs keyed on mix.lock. The repo currently has no CI at all — this is the single largest automation gap. Integration tests stay excluded by default (they need Moderato/Stripe/Sepolia credentials); leave a commented opt-in job or note for a credentialed integration run.

task.title: Unit tests for MultiProvider and ConCacheStore
acceptance_criteria: multi_provider_test.exs covers first-match, no-match, and config pass-through
con_cache_store_test.exs covers get/put, TTL expiry, check_and_mark atomicity
Both modules reach the standard 80% coverage tier
Tests fail loudly on unexpected outcomes (no assert-true-on-error)
task.body: Close the two direct-unit-test gaps surfaced in the 2026-06-12 health review. Add test/mpp/client/multi_provider_test.exs covering MPP.Client.MultiProvider first-match routing across [{module, config}] entries, the no-match path, and config pass-through to the chosen provider. Add test/mpp/tempo/con_cache_store_test.exs covering MPP.Tempo.ConCacheStore get/put, TTL expiry, and check_and_mark atomicity (the atomic dedup path). Both modules currently have zero direct tests; adding them also satisfies the coverage-before-mutating gate for any future change to either.

task.title: Public API @doc + missing @spec pass
acceptance_criteria: @doc on all listed modules' public functions
All missing @spec annotations filled (def and defp per project mandate)
mix doctor passes with raised doc coverage
No IO in @doc examples
task.body: Documentation pass flagged by the 2026-06-12 health review: most public functions carry @moduledoc but no per-function @doc. Add @doc to public functions across amount.ex, body_digest.ex, challenge.ex, credential.ex, errors.ex, headers.ex, plug.ex, receipt.ex, verifier.ex, intents/charge.ex, methods/stripe.ex, methods/tempo.ex, methods/evm.ex, methods/tempo/session_receipt.ex, mcp.ex, and client/transport/http.ex. Fill the ~15 missing @spec annotations (mcp.ex has 8 missing; method.ex, amount.ex, intents/charge.ex, tempo.ex, transport/http.ex have the rest). Follow the no-IO-in-@doc-examples convention. Run mix doctor to confirm doc/spec coverage rises.
